Pryvitne Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Volyn Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This is the old cemetery of Pryvitne (formerly Svynyukhy), presumably dating to the 17th or 18th century, serving a community first mentioned in the late 16th century and subordinate to the kehilla of Ludmir (Volodymyr-Volynsky, documented elsewhere in this collection); by 1700, the community included 100 taxed families. The population reached 629 (35 percent) by 1897, declining to 173 by 1921 amid WWI-era displacement, with most remaining families belonging to the Olyka and Trisk Hasidic branches. By October 1941, all local Jews had been sent to the Lokachi ghetto, documented elsewhere in this collection, and were murdered there on September 13, 1942.
